title: Introduce retry DSL compiler and ergonomic pullstream helpers across SDKs
author: Rohan Patel
description: Motivation: multiple SDK teams requested a single source of truth for retry behavior and lightweight streaming ergonomics to reduce duplication and ensure parity across Python/TS/Go. This PR introduces a small, language-agnostic "retry DSL" and a compiler that emits typed bindings and compact runtime profiles for each SDK; it also ships a thin ergonomic pullstream helper in the TypeScript SDK plus compatibility shims for Python and Go. Work done: implemented a declarative retry policy language (backoff schedules, transient classifier predicates, idempotency hints); added a compiler tool (ts-node driven) that generates typed enums and presets for retries; extended the TS SDK with a new PullStream.peekable/resume helpers and a small AsyncCursor type that simplifies backpressure in user code; added a lease-based token provider interface to support short-lived rotating credentials and a small shim to make existing token providers backward-compatible; bumped SDK versions to publish the new artifacts. Scope: the changes are intentionally conservative at runtime: generated retry profiles are advisory to the SDKs, runtime fallback exists to previous behavior if a generated profile is incompatible. The change reduces boilerplate for customers implementing robust retries and makes streaming ergonomics more consistent across languages. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by ENG-1593 stakeholders; - [x] Compiler emits TS/Go/Python bindings; - [x] Unit tests for compiler and runtime adapters; - [x] Integration smoke tests against the hosted inference mock; - [x] Changelogs and upgrade notes included; - [x] Version bumps staged for TS@2.4.0, Py@1.9.0, Go@1.5.2 Notes on backwards compatibility: existing SDK consumers keep previous APIs; the new token lease provider is additive and can be gradually adopted. Release considerations: small window for ecosystem publishing required before client teams roll out. See linked Linear tickets ENG-1593 and ENG-1602 for rollout plan and gating criteria.
